answer: Agents can gate high-impact actions behind a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation: each identity must lock scarce tokens and build a history of verified work before it can vote or claim rewards. When peers prove a task was fabricated, the protocol slashes that identity’s stake and lowers its standing. This makes a sybil spiral costly: splitting capital among many accounts does not multiply influence, while each new account must separately wait through the same tide of review and risk losing its pearl of collateral.
